quote: Clearly, such an analysis needs to take into account not only how a system responds to an attack, but also the behavior of the attackers attempting to cause security intrusions. Both these aspects are random phenomena
locator: p. 169 printed (PDF p. 3), Sec. 1.1; also Sec. 2.2, p. 173 printed (PDF p. 7): "this time or effort 2 is best modeled as a random variable"
issue: Survives the adversarial read for the bare claim: Madan et al. say the attacker's behaviour is a random phenomenon and its time or effort is best modelled as a random variable.

claim: Madan et al. support timing tactics with exponential delays (the citation closes the sentence that justifies the exponential delay).
quote: Since the memoryless property of exponential distribution implies the absence of aging and learning, it does not seem appropriate for modeling attacker behavior.
locator: p. 185 printed (PDF p. 19), Sec. 6; also Sec. 2.2, p. 173 printed (PDF p. 7): "The above discussion suggests that we need to consider non-exponential type of distributions."
issue: Madan et al. reject the exponential distribution for attacker behaviour and build a semi-Markov model to allow non-exponential times; cited in the sentence that justifies exponential delays, the citation reads as support for the choice its source argues against.
fix_text: Same fix as holm2014 on this unit: let the citation carry only randomness, or own the departure, e.g. "... although Madan et al. argue the exponential's memorylessness suits attacker behaviour poorly~\citep{madan2004}" (this would also belong in Section 6.5's threats).
